items.title: feat(fleet-queue): surface at_cap_queued in queue health (#6528)
items.body: Fixes the surfacing branch of #6528 (criteria 2/3). Queue task 11461, routed by triage task 11211. ## What `fleet queue health` could not distinguish "queued and claimable" from "queued but every task at its attempt cap" — the dead-in-queue state behind #6528 read as ordinary backlog, and a claim coming back empty was undiagnosable from health output. The Turso health verb (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue.rs`) now computes, per queue, **at_cap_queued**: tasks with `status='queued' AND attempts >= max_attempts` — exactly the set the claim query can never return (claim requires `attempts < max_attempts`). When `at_cap_queued == queued > 0`, nothing in that queue is claimable. ## How - Separate grouped query in `verb_health` (the status GROUP BY cannot express the attempts predicate), folded into the health rows by the pure helper `apply_at_cap_queued`. - The zeroed health-row template is factored into `health_entry`, which now includes `at_cap_queued` right after `queued`. The client renders the table from row keys, so the new column appears with no client change. The PostgREST health path reads `repo_queue_health?select=*`, so it will surface the same field if the view gains it; the live backend is Turso, implemented here. ## Tests `cargo test -p fleet-queue --features queue-broker --lib` — 85 passed, including two new tests: - `health_entry_defaults_at_cap_queued_to_zero` - `at_cap_fold_covers_zero_claimable_and_partial_queues` — the #6528 fixture: a queue with queued=3 / at_cap=3 (zero claimable), a partial queue (5/2), and a queue with none at cap (stays 0). Out of scope (unchanged, per the packet): claimant launch (#6533, #6865), claim semantics, attempt counting, per-task cap raises. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(id): refuse trailing bytes in CollabMessage::decode
items.body: Fixes #6349 `CollabMessage::decode` used `rmp_serde::from_slice`, which stops after the first MessagePack value and ignores the rest. items.title: fix(id): enforce participant limit on journal restore (#2958)
items.body:
## Summary

```text
restore Issued entry
  active = count(non-revoked capabilities)
  reject when active >= participant limit
  insert capability
```

The check runs in journal order, so an earlier revocation frees capacity for a later issuance. Added coverage for over-limit and at-limit journals, issue/revoke/issue, and compacted checkpoint restore.

Closes #2958

## Evidence

- Before: restore accepted three active participants with a configured limit of two (confirmed by the #2958 triage probe).
- After: `cargo test -p id world` on the task worktree reported 388 passed; all four new restore-limit tests passed; one seccomp test failed with Zig `AppDataDirUnavailable`; 1223 tests were filtered. The isolated seccomp test passed 1/1 on clean main at `cc819feb8`, so the failure was not reproduced there; the full suite was not rerun.
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check src/world/core.rs src/world/tests.rs` — pass.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way.

**Blast Radius:** Narrow — journal restore rejects only entries that would exceed the active participant limit; revocation order and valid at-limit journals remain supported.

items.title: fix(mcpx): refuse cross-origin credential redirects
items.body: ## Summary ```text redirect from original request same normalized origin (scheme/host/effective port) → follow as before different origin → return the 3xx response (http.ErrUseLastResponse) ``` The policy covers Streamable HTTP POST/DELETE, stream GET, legacy SSE initial GET, and legacy SSE POST. Same-origin redirects retain configured headers. ## Evidence - **Before:** httptest regressions reproduced Go following cross-origin 302/307 responses and reaching the second server with the configured `X-API-Key`. - **After:** the redirect tests verify the target is not reached and the 3xx is explicit; a same-origin redirect still forwards the header. - `go test ./internal/mcpclient -count=1 -run 'Redirect|TestHTTPSSETransport|TestServerRequestCarriesTheOriginatingCallsContext|TestExtraHeadersReachTheRequest|TestEachHTTPTransportOwnsItsConnectionPool|TestCloseSessionDoesNotReissueAServerStatus'` — pass.\n- `go test ./internal/pool -count=1 -run TestAuthReachesTheUpstream` — pass.\n- `go test -race -shuffle=on -count=5 ./internal/mcpclient -run 'Redirect|TestSameHTTPOriginNormalizesSchemeHostAndDefaultPort'` — pass.\n- `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/mcpclient` — pass.\n\n## Merge Danger\n\n**Door:** two-way\n\n**Blast Radius:** low\n\nOnly cross-origin redirects change behavior: callers receive the redirect response instead of sending credentials to another origin. Same-origin redirects are unchanged.\n\nCloses #5744 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(id/web): surface withheld-step sync wedge and test multi-chunk ACK flush (#4324)
items.body: Closes #4324. Two gaps left over from the 2026-11-02 chunking work (#4051/#4052): 1. **Withheld-step path was console-only.** When `stepBatch` returns an empty batch because the head pending step alone exceeds `MAX_STEPS_MESSAGE_BYTES`, `handleEditorChange` logged to the console and returned. The local document kept the edit, but the UI showed nothing: sync had silently stopped. It now calls `updateStatus("error")` as well, so the wedge is user-visible while the edit stays in the local document (unchanged behaviour otherwise). 2. **No connection-level test for the ACK-driven flush.** Added a `FakeWebSocket` test that drives one editor change of 1,200 ~1.1 KB steps (over the byte budget), then asserts: - the first `STEPS` message is one capped batch (under `MAX_STEPS_PER_MESSAGE` and under the 1 MiB frame budget), - the second batch is **not** sent until the `UPDATE` ACK for the first, - the second batch continues in order and both batches together equal the original steps exactly once (none dropped or duplicated), - ACKing the last batch leaves nothing pending. Also added a test for the withheld path: no frame is sent, the status callback sees `error`, the console detail remains, and the local document keeps the edit. Out of scope and unchanged: splitting a single step, the server caps (`MAX_FRAME_BYTES` / `MAX_STEPS_MESSAGE_BYTES` / `MAX_STEPS_PER_MESSAGE`), server-side collab code, and the documented >1 MiB single-step limitation. ## Verification - `cd pkgs/id/web && bun run test` — 27 files, 632 passed, 9 skipped. - `tsc --noEmit` in `pkgs/id/web` — one pre-existing unrelated error in `src/image-upload.test.ts:428` (`Plugin | null`), present on `origin/main`. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix: allow opencode service first start without env file
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #5933. Allow the OpenCode service's required materializer to run on first start, when its EnvironmentFile is absent:

```text
ExecStartPre: materialize both keys
  → EnvironmentFile is optional only while absent
  → ExecStart reads the newly written file
```

The pre-start remains mandatory, so failed key materialization still blocks the server.

## Evidence

- **Before:** a transient user unit with a mandatory missing EnvironmentFile failed with result `resources`; its ExecStartPre did not run.
- **After:** the same transient test with the optional EnvironmentFile ran ExecStartPre, and ExecStart confirmed both dummy key names were loaded (values were not printed).
- `nix-instantiate --parse home/common/default.nix` passed.
- Host drvPath evaluation passed for both `amd` and `nixos`.
- Current running service has both key names in its process environment and the file mode is 0600. The full system switch / live absent-file test was not run; the full switch requires sudo.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** low

Only this service's EnvironmentFile is made optional; the materializer remains a required ExecStartPre.

items.title: test(ready-for-agent): make apply-config test hermetic to runner DRY_RUN env (salvage #7475)
items.body: Salvage of the functional remainder of closed archive PR #7475 (task 14188, routed from triage task 13800 on issue #7297). PR #7475 itself is not reopened; its head was the diff source. ## What `pm-stack/ready-for-agent/test-apply-config.sh`: the first and second ("normal") applies ran as plain `./apply-config.sh`, inheriting the test runner's environment. An exported `DRY_RUN=1`/`true` silently turned both into dry runs. This change applies the PR #7475 remainder, adapted to current main: - `unset DRY_RUN` guard (with its comment) after the `RFA_*` exports — "Do not let the test runner's environment affect the normal-apply cases." - First apply runs as `DRY_RUN=0 ./apply-config.sh`; its ok line names that. - Second apply runs as `env -u DRY_RUN ./apply-config.sh`. The PR-era header-comment rewrite is deliberately NOT carried: main has since added cases the old header does not describe (`DRY_RUN=TrUe` case-insensitivity, a dedicated `DRY_RUN=0` falsey case), so the header on main is the current one. ## Verification - Repro on clean main (fe5d6eafe9): `DRY_RUN=1 bash ./test-apply-config.sh` → exit 1, failing at the first apply (no `addLocalRepository` mutation); clean env → PASS. - With this change: PASS in clean env, with `DRY_RUN=1` exported, and with `DRY_RUN=true` exported (`apply-config.test: PASS` in all three). Refs #7297 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: ci(auto-format): retry after main push races
items.body: ## Summary ```text for each bounded format pass fetch/reset to latest origin/main recompute changed files and run treefmt push the fresh formatter commit if main advanced, discard stale output and retry ``` A rejected push now triggers a fresh formatting pass instead of rebasing a formatter commit that may conflict with concurrent edits. Push failures without a main advance fail immediately; three consecutive races fail without recording a success SHA so the next scheduled run retries. Adds a regression test injecting a concurrent edit to `pm-stack/aggregator/README.md` and verifying the retry preserves and formats the newer main content. Fixes #5230 ## Evidence - **Before:** the new race regression failed on the old workflow after `git pull --rebase origin main` hit the expected README conflict. - **After:** `python3 -I -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_auto_format_workflow.py' -v` — 6 passed. - `nix run .#format-check -- .github/workflows/auto-format.yml scripts/tests/test_auto_format_workflow.py` — pass. - `actionlint .github/workflows/auto-format.yml` — pass. - `git diff --check` — pass. ## Merge Danger **Door:** Two-way; reverting the workflow and regression test restores the previous retry behavior. **Blast Radius:** Low — scheduled auto-format workflow only. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: id(directory_auth): refuse out-of-domain nonces in sign_request (#6443)
items.body: Fixes #6443. `sign_request` now returns `Result` and refuses an empty nonce, one over 64 chars, or one with a character outside ASCII alphanumeric plus `-` — the same domain `verify_signed` enforces (shared `nonce_in_domain` helper). No change to verify verdicts, wire format, replay guard or time window. Tests: new `sign_request_refuses_nonces_verify_signed_would_reject` pins each refusal class and that valid controls (short, `abc-DEF-123`, 64 chars) still verify. Existing callers updated with `.unwrap()`. Verified by CI; local build not completed. Queue task 10889. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.
